lesson.title: Prerequisites: what each model really needs
lesson.lead: Only two earlier topics feed SVM. Most models need just the first one, so you can start SVM before KKT.

items: **P1 · Vectors:** dot product wᵀx, length ‖w‖, and the distance |wᵀx + b| / ‖w‖ from a point to a line. MFML `Lecture_3.pdf` (inner products, norms). Needed by **every** model.

**P2 · Lagrange multipliers and KKT:** Lagrangian, the four KKT conditions, the dual. MFML `Lecture_11.pdf` and `Lecture_14.pdf`, plus `Lagrange-KKT-Duality-Practice-Set.pdf`. Needed **only** for M3, M8 and the KKT proof in M2.

blocks.label: How to use the time
blocks.text: Each board ends with a **fastest path**: the slide pages and Sourabh sir's sections to read, the problems to do, and **at most one video, only if you're stuck**. The SVM Companion (`Prof. Saurabh/practice_problems/Support_Vector_Machines_Companion.pdf`) already explains every model with proofs, so read it before any video. Whole chapter: about 7 hours, with no video needed.

lesson.title: P1 · Vectors: dot product, norm, distance to a line
lesson.lead: Needed by all 8 models. Source: MFML `Lecture_3.pdf`.

blocks.text: wᵀx = w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + … + wₙxₙ     ‖w‖ = √(wᵀw)
blocks.caption: Example: (3, 4)ᵀ(4, 2) = 20, ‖(3, 4)‖ = 5

blocks.text: distance of x₀ from wᵀx + b = 0  =  |wᵀx₀ + b| / ‖w‖
blocks.caption: So the margin lines wᵀx + b = ±1 are each 1/‖w‖ from the boundary

items: The sign of wᵀx + b says which side of the line x is on: that is the SVM prediction.
w is perpendicular to the line wᵀx + b = 0.

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 25 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_3.pdf` p. 4–5 (norms, inner products), p. 9 (lengths and distances); `Lecture_14.pdf` p. 12–13 (hyperplane); SVM Companion §2 (w is perpendicular to the boundary, distance formula).
**Do:** the quick check on the previous board.
**Video, only if stuck:** [3Blue1Brown · Dot products and duality](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LyGKycYT2v0), only if wᵀx still feels like just arithmetic.

lesson.title: P2 · Lagrange multipliers and KKT
lesson.lead: Needed only for M3 (dual), M8 (kernel SVM) and the KKT proof in M2. Source: MFML `Lecture_11.pdf`, `Lecture_14.pdf`.

blocks.text: L(x, λ) = f(x) + Σ λᵢ gᵢ(x),  gᵢ(x) ≤ 0,  λᵢ ≥ 0

items: **Stationarity:** ∇f + Σλᵢ∇gᵢ = 0
**Primal feasibility:** gᵢ(x) ≤ 0
**Dual feasibility:** λᵢ ≥ 0
**Complementary slackness:** λᵢgᵢ(x) = 0, so λᵢ > 0 only on an active constraint (in SVM: only support vectors have α > 0)

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 45 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_11.pdf` p. 20–22 (Lagrangian, primal and dual); `Lecture_14.pdf` p. 3–4 and 8–11 (weak and strong duality, Slater, KKT); SVM Companion §6.2 (the four KKT conditions).
**Do:** Solved Practice Set P37 (verify KKT), KKT set P15 (tiny SVM capstone).
**Video, only if stuck:** [Visualizing KKT conditions](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yDMlNumgZ9E), only if complementary slackness (λ·g = 0) is not clear.

lesson.title: M1 · Hard-margin primal, separating line, margin
lesson.lead: Priority 3. Feb 2026 Q5 (8 marks), the newest paper. Saurabh sir has 5 problems on it.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: P1: dot product, ‖w‖, distance to a line.

**They give:** a small 2-D dataset and one or two candidate lines. **They ask:** the primal with one constraint per point, show each line separates the data, the margin of each line, which is bigger, and classify new points.
min ½(w₁² + w₂²)   s.t.  yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1  for every point
blocks.caption: Write all constraints out with the numbers substituted: that is where the marks are

items: **Separates:** put every point into wᵀx + b. The sign must match its label for every point.
**Margin:** distance from a point to the line is |wᵀxᵢ + b| ÷ ‖w‖. The line's margin is the smallest distance over all points.
Compare the two margins. The larger one is the better line.
**Classify** a new point by the sign of wᵀx + b.

blocks.label: Exam trap
blocks.text: 1/‖w‖ is the margin only after scaling w, b so that the closest point has |wᵀx + b| = 1. 2/‖w‖ is the full width between the two margin lines. Say which one you are giving.

items: Saurabh sir: **P44** (which line has the bigger margin), **P46** (verify a claimed solution), **Practice Paper Q6** (5M), **Companion Q7** (verify a hyperplane by KKT), **Q15** (geometric margin).

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 60 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_14.pdf` p. 20–24 (linear classifier); SVM Companion §1–5 (why maximise the margin, one inequality replaces two, the convex QP).
**Do:** P44, P46, Practice Paper Q6, then Feb 2026 Q5 timed (8 marks, 28 min).
**Video, only if stuck:** [StatQuest · SVM Part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efR1C6CvhmE), only if you can't picture the margin. Otherwise skip.

lesson.title: M6 · Kernel matrix
lesson.lead: Priority 5. 9 marks: 2023 regular Q2B (3), 2023 DS makeup Q2B (3, the same question), Sep 2025 Q6b (3). Quick marks.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: P1 only: a kernel value is a dot product.
Kᵢⱼ = k(xᵢ, xⱼ) = φ(xᵢ)ᵀφ(xⱼ)
blocks.caption: N points give an N × N symmetric matrix. The diagonal entries are ‖φ(xᵢ)‖²

blocks.label: Exam trap
blocks.text: Compute only the upper triangle and copy it across, but write the full matrix in the answer.

items: Saurabh sir: part (a) of **P49**, **P50**, **Practice Paper Q7**, **Companion Q1, Q2**.

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 15 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_14.pdf` p. 14–16 (kernel functions and their property); SVM Companion §11.7 (the kernel matrix).
**Do:** 2023 Q2B and Sep 2025 Q6b (both 3 marks).
**Video, only if stuck:** No video: the slides and the companion cover it.

lesson.title: M7 · Feature map ↔ kernel
lesson.lead: Priority 2. 14.5 marks: 2022 makeup Q4(2) (5), Sep 2024 regular Q(B) (5, the same question), Sep 2025 Q6a (3), 2023 DS regular Q2B (1.5).

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: P1 (dot product), expanding (a + b)², and M6 (what a kernel value is).
**They give:** a kernel and ask for φ (with its dimension), or a φ and ask for its kernel, or ask you to show that φ produces k.

items: Expand the kernel into a sum of products of x-terms and z-terms.
Each term ax_i x_j·z_i z_j becomes the feature √a·x_i x_j (and the same with z).
Write φ(x) as one long vector and count its entries for the dimension.
Check: φ(x)ᵀφ(z) must give back every term of k.

blocks.text: (xᵀz)² + 3(xᵀz + 2)² = 4(xᵀz)² + 12·xᵀz + 12
blocks.caption: The repeated question. φ = [2x_i x_j for all i, j (n² entries), √12·x_i (n entries), √12] has dimension n² + n + 1

blocks.text: φ(x) = [1, √2·x, x²]  ⇒  φ(x)ᵀφ(z) = 1 + 2xz + x²z² = (1 + xz)²
blocks.caption: Sep 2025 Q6a, 3 marks

blocks.label: Exam trap
blocks.text: (xᵀz)ᵖ (homogeneous) and (xᵀz + 1)ᵖ (non-homogeneous) use different feature counts. Companion Q12 drills the two counting formulas.

items: Saurabh sir: **P51** (feature map behind a polynomial kernel), **Companion Q12** (feature counting), **Q13** (verify the kernel identity).

blocks.text: Fastest path (about 40 min)

items: **Read:** `Lecture_14.pdf` p. 17–18 (constructing kernels); SVM Companion §11.5–11.6 (the kernels you meet, how many features).
**Do:** P51, Companion Q12, Q13, then the repeated question (2022 makeup Q4(2) = Sep 2024 Q(B)).
**Video, only if stuck:** [StatQuest · SVM Part 2: Polynomial kernel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Toet3EiSFcM), only if expanding (xᵀz + c)² into φ(x)ᵀφ(z) is unclear.

worked.title: Hard margin · Feb 2026 Q5: two separating lines (8 marks)

problem.text: X1 (2, 2) +1, X2 (4, 4) +1, X3 (2, 0) −1, X4 (4, 0) −1. (a) Write the hard-margin primal. [2M] (b) Show x₂ = 1 separates the data. [2M] (c) Show x₂ − x₁ = −1 separates the data. [2M] (d) Find the margin of each and say which is better. [2M]

steps.label: (a) Primal
steps.text:
min ½(w₁² + w₂²) subject to one constraint per point, yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b) ≥ 1:
- 2w₁ + 2w₂ + b ≥ 1
- 4w₁ + 4w₂ + b ≥ 1
- −(2w₁ + b) ≥ 1
- −(4w₁ + b) ≥ 1
[1M objective, 1M the four constraints]

steps.label: (b) x₂ = 1
steps.text:
Write it as x₂ − 1 = 0, so w = (0, 1), b = −1, f(x) = x₂ − 1.
X1: 1 > 0, X2: 3 > 0 (both +1 ✓). X3: −1 < 0, X4: −1 < 0 (both −1 ✓). Every sign matches its label, so it separates.

steps.label: (d) Margins
steps.text:
The key uses margin = 1/‖w‖ (each line is already scaled so the closest points give |f| = 1).
x₂ = 1: ‖w‖ = 1 ⇒ margin **1**.
x₂ − x₁ = −1: ‖w‖ = √2 ⇒ margin 1/√2 ≈ **0.7071**.
1 > 0.7071, so **x₂ = 1 is the better separator**.

worked.answer: Both lines separate the data; margins 1 and 0.7071, so x₂ = 1 is better.

worked.title: Hard margin · Practice Paper Q6: verify a solver's answer (5 marks)

problem.text: Training data: (2, 2)+, (4, 3)+, (0, 0)−, (−1, 0)−. A solver returns w = (½, ½), b = −1. (a) Primal with its four constraints. [1M] (b) Check every constraint, name the support vectors, find the αᵢ from KKT. [2M] (c) Margin 1/‖w‖. [1M] (d) Classify (3, 0) and (1, 0.5). [1M]

steps.label: (a) Primal
steps.text: min ½(w₁² + w₂²) s.t. 2w₁ + 2w₂ + b ≥ 1, 4w₁ + 3w₂ + b ≥ 1, −b ≥ 1, −(−w₁ + b) ≥ 1.

steps.label: (b) Check
steps.text: yᵢ(wᵀxᵢ + b): (2, 2) → 1; (4, 3) → 2.5; (0, 0) → 1; (−1, 0) → 1.5. All ≥ 1, so feasible. The value is exactly 1 for **(2, 2) and (0, 0)**: those are the support vectors.

steps.label: (b) α from KKT
steps.text: Non-support vectors get α = 0: α₂ = α₄ = 0. With α₁ = α₃ = α (from Σαᵢyᵢ = 0): w = α(2, 2) − α(0, 0) = (2α, 2α) = (½, ½) ⇒ **α = ¼**.

worked.title: Kernels · Sep 2025 Q6: (1 + xz)² and a 4×4 kernel matrix (6 marks)

problem.text: 1-D data x = [−1.5, −0.5, 0.5, 1.5], y = [1, −1, −1, 1] (not linearly separable). Feature map φ(x) = [1, √2·x, x²]. (a) Show the kernel is k(x, z) = (1 + xz)². [3M] (b) Compute the 4×4 kernel matrix Kᵢⱼ = k(xᵢ, xⱼ). [3M]

steps.label: (b) Products xᵢxⱼ
steps.text: x₁x₁ = x₄x₄ = 2.25; x₂x₂ = x₃x₃ = 0.25; x₁x₂ = x₃x₄ = 0.75; x₁x₃ = x₂x₄ = −0.75; x₁x₄ = −2.25; x₂x₃ = −0.25.

steps.label: Why it helps
steps.text: In feature space the x² coordinate is 2.25 for the +1 points and 0.25 for the −1 points, so the plane x² = 1.25 (|x| = 1.118) separates them.

worked.answer: k = (1 + xz)²; K as in the table (symmetric, diagonal 10.5625, 1.5625, 1.5625, 10.5625).

worked.title: Kernels · 2022 makeup Q4(2) = Sep 2024 Q(B): find φ for a sum of kernels (5 marks)

problem.text: K(x, z) = (xᵀz)² + 3(xᵀz + 2)² for x, z ∈ ℝⁿ. If possible, find φ: ℝⁿ → ℝ^(n² + n + 1) with K(x, z) = φ(x)ᵀφ(z).

steps.label: Expand
steps.text: (xᵀz)² + 3[(xᵀz)² + 4xᵀz + 4] = **4(xᵀz)² + 12xᵀz + 12**.

steps.label: Quadratic part
steps.text: 4(xᵀz)² = ΣᵢΣⱼ 4xᵢxⱼzᵢzⱼ = ΣᵢΣⱼ (2xᵢxⱼ)(2zᵢzⱼ) ⇒ φ₁(x) = [2xᵢxⱼ for all i, j]: **n²** entries.

steps.label: Linear part
steps.text: 12xᵀz = Σ (√12 xᵢ)(√12 zᵢ) ⇒ φ₂(x) = [√12 x₁, …, √12 xₙ]: **n** entries.

steps.label: Answer
steps.text: φ(x) = [φ₁(x), φ₂(x), φ₃(x)] has n² + n + 1 entries and φ(x)ᵀφ(z) = K(x, z). So the mapping exists.

worked.answer: φ(x) = [2xᵢxⱼ (all i, j), √12·xᵢ, √12], dimension n² + n + 1.

worked.title: Kernels · 2023 Q2B: kernel matrix with a ‖x‖ feature (3 marks)

problem.text: X = [(4, −3), (0, 1)], φ(x) = [x₁, x₂, ‖x‖]ᵀ. Compute the kernel matrix K.

worked.title: Kernels · 2023 DS regular Q2B: dimension and kernel of a cubic feature map (1.5 marks)

problem.text: φ(x) = [1, x₁, …, xₘ, x₁³, …, xₘ³, x₁x₂x₃, x₂x₃x₄, …, xₘ₋₂xₘ₋₁xₘ]ᵀ. Find the dimension of the transformed data and the kernel K(x, y).

steps.label: Kernel
steps.text: K(x, y) = φ(x)ᵀφ(y) = 1 + Σxᵢyᵢ + Σxᵢ³yᵢ³ + Σ xᵢxᵢ₊₁xᵢ₊₂·yᵢyᵢ₊₁yᵢ₊₂ (i = 1 … m − 2) [1M].
